recent_posts.title: Build a deep research tool
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a command-line deep research tool using the Browserbase SDK for web search and page fetching, combined with OpenAI for summarization. The tool searches the web via Browserbase's search API, fetches up to 30 unique URLs, deduplicates and diversifies sources, then summarizes findings into a markdown report. The TypeScript project is open source, configurable via environment variables, and costs roughly $1 per 1,000 pages fetched. The author also outlines a multi-loop agentic pattern where synthesis results feed back into new searches.

recent_posts.title: Building a $10k desktop app with AI agents without opening an IDE
recent_posts.summary: A 20-year software developer built SoloTerm, a desktop terminal workspace for managing AI agents and long-running dev commands, earning nearly $11,000 in revenue. Built over 3-4 months with 951 commits using AI coding agents but without opening an IDE, the author argues this is 'agentic engineering' not 'vibe coding' — because they actively supervised every agent action, directed refactoring, enforced testing and CI, and kept hands on the wheel. The post demonstrates SoloTerm's features (multi-project management, agent tabs, MCP server integration, auto-summarization) and warns that unsupervised AI agents quickly produce sloppy, uncontrollable codebases.

recent_posts.title: Google Stitch demo for non-designers building websites with AI
recent_posts.summary: Google Stitch is an AI-powered design tool that generates UI designs, design systems, and responsive code from prompts. The author demos creating a personal website by generating multiple layout variations, iterating on a design system that cascades changes across all designs, and exporting code or a design.md file to hand off to AI coding tools like Claude Code or Codex. While initial outputs can look templated, iterating with prompts yields polished results. The conclusion is that designers aren't being replaced — they'll use tools like this to move faster.

recent_posts.title: Your new agentic development environment
recent_posts.summary: Solo is a desktop application serving as a lightweight agentic development environment. It lets developers manage multiple projects with configurable commands, auto-start/restart processes, and integrated AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Cline, Aider). Key features include a solo.yaml config file committable to repos for team onboarding, auto-summarization of terminal/agent output using cheap LLM models, an MCP server allowing agents to read neighboring process logs, desktop notifications, local-only command storage for secrets, and extensive UI customization. Free tier covers up to 4 projects and 20 processes.

recent_posts.title: YouTube channel restructuring for Laravel, PHP and database content
recent_posts.summary: A content creator announces channel restructuring to improve content organization and algorithm performance. The main channel will focus on Laravel, PHP, and web development, while database education content moves to a dedicated 'Database School' channel, and database interviews get their own podcast channel. The creator believes this separation will help YouTube's algorithm better target appropriate audiences for each content type.

recent_posts.title: Pixel Table combines database functionality with AI data processing workflows
recent_posts.summary: Marcel Corner, creator of Apache Impala and co-creator of Apache Parquet, discusses his new company Pixel Table, a multimodal database designed for AI workloads. The system combines traditional ACID-compliant database functionality with the ability to handle videos, images, documents, and other unstructured data types. Pixel Table allows users to define computational workflows through computed columns and iterators, automatically managing data transformations like video transcription, chunking, and embedding generation. The platform addresses the data plumbing challenges faced by AI teams who currently rely on fragmented scripts and multiple systems to process multimodal data for model training and inference.

recent_posts.title: Sharding Postgres without extensions with PgDog founder, Lev Kokotov
recent_posts.summary: Lev Kokotov, founder of PgDog, discusses building a PostgreSQL sharding solution that operates as a standalone application rather than an extension. PgDog sits in front of PostgreSQL instances, providing transparent sharding without requiring application changes. Unlike Citus (which runs inside PostgreSQL), PgDog runs externally and can scale horizontally, targeting OLTP workloads with lower latency. The system uses PostgreSQL's SQL parser for query compatibility while implementing its own query routing and result aggregation. Kokotov explains the migration process using logical replication to move from single instances to sharded setups, and shares insights about building database infrastructure companies, including the challenges of extensions versus standalone applications for distribution and adoption.

recent_posts.title: Programming by wishful thinking with Laravel traits
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their approach of 'programming by wishful thinking' where they first imagine and write code for a desired Laravel feature (models that use traits), then implement the actual functionality afterward. This creative process demonstrates how developers can drive innovation by starting with the ideal API they want to use.

recent_posts.title: Programming by wishful thinking
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates "programming by wishful thinking" - writing the desired API first, then implementing it. Shows how to create a Laravel trait for vector embeddings with abstract methods, build a reflection-based system to find models using specific traits, and develop a flexible ReflectionCollection class for introspecting PHP classes. The approach emphasizes starting with clean, readable interfaces before tackling the underlying implementation details.
